md_docs_2zalgo(3) Library Functions Manual md_docs_2zalgo(3)

NAME

md_docs_2zalgo - Zalgo terminal effect

--zalgo decorates the displayed video with Unicode combining marks. It is available in mirror, client, and discovery modes. Omit the option to disable it. 

ascii-chat mirror --test-pattern --zalgo
ascii-chat mirror --zalgo=1
ascii-chat mirror --webcam-index 1 --zalgo=10

Bare --zalgo uses intensity 7. Both --zalgo=7 and --zalgo 7 select an explicit intensity. Values must be integers from 1 to 10. A following session name is not consumed as the optional number. ASCII_CHAT_ZALGO accepts 1-10.

Intensity Coverage of eligible characters Marks per affected character 1 3% 1 2 6% 1 3 10% 1 4 18% 1 5 28% 1-2 6 40% 1-3 7 55% 2-4 8 70% 3-5 9 85% 4-7 10 100% 6-10

Positions and mark choices remain stable between frames. Increasing intensity adds marks without reshuffling the pattern. Only printable ASCII characters other than spaces are decorated. Existing Unicode, spaces, colors, and control sequences are preserved. REP compression is expanded before adding marks.

Use a UTF-8 terminal and a font with combining-mark support. On Windows, run chcp 65001 in the terminal before starting ascii-chat. Stacking and clipping vary by terminal and font; high levels deliberately obscure the image.

--utf8=true overrides automatic detection. --utf8=false is incompatible with Zalgo, including piped snapshots. If decoration would exceed the presenter's 16 MiB frame limit (including cursor controls), the original frame is displayed and a rate-limited warning is logged.

The effect applies locally to terminal output and text snapshots, including --strip-ansi output. It does not modify network frames, logs, status screens, or --render-file video exports. Half-block and other Unicode palettes retain their original glyphs, so use --render-mode foreground for ASCII decoration.

Browser rendering

The web app offers Zalgo: Off / Level 1-10 in Settings for Mirror, Client, and Discovery. The level is saved in the URL (?zalgo=7). The website's display effects demo starts at 7 and offers all ten levels with the demo video or webcam.

Browser canvases reuse the native distribution and mark selection. A separate combining font is composited after all cell backgrounds, so marks can cross rows and work alongside Matrix without being erased. The precise glyph stacking can differ from a terminal's font shaping. This is a local display effect; network frames are unchanged.
